reason: Sources: experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_P/report.txt and report.json (folds[*].eval.per_embryo), out_full_Q/report.txt, experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md sec. 1 and 4, CONTEXT.md. The cited numbers are correct. The inference from them does not hold. (1) The -19% in-domain gain is a 6bba effect, not a general one. Pooling the per-embryo leak5 OOF over the 5 folds gives: 6bba none 1.720 / public 1.567 / P 1.219 um (-22% vs public); 44b6 none 1.499 / public 1.296 / P 1.343 um, i.e. P is 3.6% WORSE than public (2.9% worse without x138's probable training videos). P loses on 44b6 in 4 of 5 folds even though 44b6 clips were in its training set. The pooled figure is 85% 6bba by weight (106k of 126k pairs), so 'P sharpens nodes 3x more' really means 'P learned how 6bba was annotated'. (2) Removing the bias does not save it. I estimated per-axis bias-free MAE with a Gaussian fit to the reported bias and MAE (rough; it assumes one bias per fold). Out of embryo, the per-node component barely transfers: 44b6->6bba P 2.072 vs none 2.079 (0%); 6bba->44b6 P 1.918 vs none 2.039 (-6%) vs public 1.845 (-9.5%). The debiased head Q, which is the Arm-B mechanism trained explicitly, also loses to public in both directions: +6.3% and +1.3% in mean distance; bias-free 1.35 vs 1.29 and 1.45 vs 1.43 um. Arm B = P minus its own mean plus public's mean, so it inherits exactly this per-node component, and that component is ~0-6% out of embryo, no better than the public head's. (3) Most of what a head contributes on the LB is the node multiplier, which the lab gate does not measure. On 6bba the public head's bias-free per-node gain is ~0 (per-axis sum 2.09-2.20 vs none 2.05-2.14 in every leak5 fold). The 7 um re-match counts move by <= 0.1% for every head. exp51 vs exp48: final nodes -2.9% -> 0.1 x 0.029 x ~0.91 = +0.0026, which is about the whole +0.002 LB gain on our stack. x138 vs readmit-v1: nodes -2.4% -> ~+0.0022 of its +0.007, and most of the drop is on one dummy clip (44b6_0b24845f -10.7%). P moves 45% of peaks by >= 1 um (public 10.5%). That pushes the position-dependent edge scorer and ILP much further from their training distribution, so the node-count change could go either way; M1-M3 cannot predict it, and a +-3% dummy node window allows +-0.003 of multiplier drift. (4) Value. The localisation-only LB response is at most ~+0.0007-0.0008 per 1% bias-free cut (x138: ~+0.0045 for ~5.7%; ours: ~0 after the multiplier). On a third embryo P_matched vs public is plausibly -4%..+4% bias-free (central ~0 to +1%, a guess bracketed by the out-of-embryo numbers above). So Arm B is about +0.0005 +- 0.003 public and Arm A about -0.001 +- 0.004, both below the +0.002 bar. The public LB also cannot separate them: public is one embryo and scores move ~0.003 run to run. Upside exists only if the hidden embryos were annotated like 6bba. Nothing supports that: the public head, balanced 10+10, transferred; a 6bba-dominated fit is the opposite bet. (5) Private (71%, other embryos): the same or worse. Arm A carries the 6bba z-convention risk (out-of-embryo z bias -0.54 um on 44b6), and Arm B carries the 6bba-specific per-node convention. Two slots and ~1.3 Vitalii GPU-h would go to a coin flip.
fix_if_any: Not as specified. A version with a chance: (a) Retrain with pairs balanced by embryo (weight 44b6 up to 50%) and with per-video debiased targets. Gate PER EMBRYO rather than pooled: in the leak5 OOF it must beat public on 44b6 AND on 6bba separately, and on both embryo-held-out directions it must beat the REPLICA-20 comparator by >= 3% on the offset-invariant GT-edge displacement error (M2). (b) Add a node-multiplier gate. The dummy-clip ILP node count must stay within +-1% of the public head's, not +-3%, or its change must be explained. Otherwise any LB delta is uninterpretable. (c) Then do not spend a dedicated probe. Ride it as a passenger only in a final that already needs a slot, and only if (a) and (b) pass. If Friend A's GPU exists, the better use of the same effort is the x138 lab replay with official scoring of the full tail (relink/readmit/gapfill) on refined vs public coordinates, which measures the quantity the LB rewards.
realistic_public_gain: Arm B (bias-matched): +0.0005 (range -0.003 .. +0.003); Arm A (raw P): -0.001 (range -0.005 .. +0.004). Both below +0.002 and inside one-embryo LB noise (~0.003). The idea's +0.005-0.009 ceiling assumes the third embryo is annotated like 6bba (P's gain is 6bba-only).
realistic_private_gain: About 0 for Arm B (-0.003 .. +0.002). Arm A is negative-skewed (-0.004 .. +0.003) because of the embryo z convention (out-of-embryo z bias -0.54 um in 6bba->44b6). Private is 71% on unseen embryos, where neither the per-node nor the offset component is shown to transfer.
critical_path: Mechanically possible: the laptop gate (CPU, ~2 h) and --force-export of P by the orchestrator on Vitalii's laptop, 25 Sep evening after #34/#35. build_probe_kernel --patch headswap with a byte-identity test (~1.5 h). Vitalii's two dummy GPU runs after 00:00 UTC 26 Sep (~40 min each). Submission ~01:00 UTC 26 Sep, scored ~08:00-11:00 UTC 26 Sep. Well before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC. Not recommended: the expected value is below the bar, and the gate as designed (pooled metrics, a +-3% node window) cannot predict the LB sign.
